findings.title: Localized parameter lookup rejects valid foundation families
findings.body: The command discovers and configures foundation types through LookupParameter("Length") and LookupParameter("Width"). LookupParameter uses localized display names and may also select an unintended parameter when names are duplicated. Consequently, valid standard families can be rejected or the wrong parameters modified under non-English Revit installations or families with ambiguous parameter names. Use stable built-in parameter identifiers where applicable, or explicitly resolve and validate configured/shared parameter definitions.

findings.title: Level-less views silently place foundations on an arbitrary level
findings.body: When ActiveView.GenLevel is null, such as in a 3D view, the command uses the first Level returned by an unordered collector. This level is not derived from the selected CAD instance or each foundation's elevation, so foundations can be associated with the wrong story and receive incorrect offsets or scheduling metadata. The command should deterministically obtain or request the intended level, or select the appropriate level from the CAD geometry elevation, and explicitly handle the case where no level exists.

findings.title: Auto-placement behavior is not implemented
findings.body: The change only introduces a passive data container. It contains no CAD geometry extraction, foundation type or level selection, coordinate transformation, validation, collision handling, or Revit element creation logic. Consequently, the supplied snapshot cannot satisfy AC-03, which requires foundations to be automatically placed from CAD data.

findings.title: Vertical CAD edges can crash extraction
findings.body: The code accepts rectangles in arbitrary 3D orientations, but then computes `BasisZ.CrossProduct(longestEdge).Normalize()`. If the longest edge is vertical or nearly vertical, the cross product is zero or numerically unstable and normalization can throw or produce invalid geometry, aborting extraction for the entire CAD import. Reject non-horizontal outlines or derive both in-plane axes from the validated polygon plane before normalizing.

findings.title: Retracing polylines are misclassified as rectangles
findings.body: Using the absolute dot product treats antiparallel consecutive segments as collinear. Combined with checking only the number of direction changes, this accepts closed outlines that reverse over an edge, self-overlap, or contain more than four effective vertices. Such malformed CAD geometry can produce a bounding-box foundation that does not match the drawn outline. The parser should reject direction reversals and validate four distinct ordered corners, non-self-intersection, and opposite-edge relationships.
